graph_review_omissions: The representation does not preserve the current Supreme Court respondent set as separate objects: Young Friends & Co., Ashu Mohan Gupta, and Shashi Gupta. This matters because the source also uses different respondent numbering for the original eviction proceeding.

The representation omits the source statement that the premises were originally rented in 1936 to the then proprietor, since deceased, of the current first respondent. That chronology is important to keeping the tenant/proprietor/firm identities separate even though it does not establish when the alleged doctor arrangements began.

The representation omits the Additional Rent Controller's specific finding that respondent no. 5, Young Friends & Co., was an entity of the respondent tenant only. This is important because it directly bears on object identity and on whether that firm was itself a separate alleged subtenant.

The representation omits the Additional Rent Controller's specific finding concerning respondent no. 6: no subletting, assignment, or parting with possession was found, and respondent no. 6 was occupying a public verandah outside the tenanted premises.

The representation does not expressly record that the Appellate Tribunal passed an eviction order on the ground of subletting; f7 records reversal and acceptance of the landlord's subletting position but omits the resulting eviction disposition.
review_omissions: No supplied law unit or proposed preference entry was omitted from the proposal; all fourteen use entries and all sixteen preference entries are reviewable from the supplied material.

The direct section 14(1)(b) proposal does not include IK-38604742:L149-L160 among its case_refs even though those passages contain the retained Appellate Tribunal's most explicit reasoning that the doctors' time-limited use amounted to exclusive possession and furnished an eviction ground. Those passages remain lower-forum reasoning and cannot be converted into a Supreme Court finding, but they are relevant to preserving the supplied disagreement.

The preference between LAW:S02:DRC:16 and LAW:V21:GR:REPORTED_DELHI is presented directionally even though the two sources address different relevant dimensions: section 16 addresses timing, lawful subletting and written consent, while the reported Delhi material addresses the breadth of assignment or other parting with possession. The supplied originals do not compel the proposed ordering.

graph_review_omissions: IK-308216:L157 states as part of the tenant-side position that Baldev Raj and Sat Pal had constituted a Hindu Undivided Family. No fact, object, or relation preserves this asserted family-unit context, which may matter when evaluating the competing account of the sons' presence and business activity.

IK-308216:L166-L167 contain an amendment-stage competing tenancy-identity and procedural account that is not preserved: the appellant contended that M/s. Bindra Tent House had taken the property on rent; the record also refers to an earlier eviction petition against the appellant and his two sons, with the respondent admitting that an earlier petition had been filed but asserting that it was improperly instituted and withdrawn. f13 preserves the Tribunal's refusal of the amendment and the prior admission that Jagan Nath was tenant, but not these underlying competing assertions.

IK-308216:L154 reports that Jagan Nath died during the Supreme Court appeal and that his sons were substituted. That procedural-stage and party-identity information is not represented, even though the same sons are also the alleged recipients of the earlier parting with possession.
review_omissions: For LAW:V21:GR:REPORTED_DELHI, the proposal's selected quote is narrower than the proposition relied on in its reason: the original also expressly says that section 14(b) is wide enough to include an assignment or any other mode by which possession is parted. The proposal's reason captures that point, but the quoted fragment alone does not.

graph_review_omissions: The representation does not fully preserve the directional and territorial detail in IK-1106992:L50: West was appointed Caravan's agent in the territory of Delhi, while Caravan was appointed West's agent for certain purposes. f15 and r3 preserve reciprocal agency generally, but omit these stated limits, which may matter when interpreting the parties' presence and operations at the disputed premises.
review_omissions: No supplied use or preference entry was omitted from the proposal; all 14 law-use entries and all 16 proposed pairwise preferences are reviewable from the supplied material.

The proposal does not isolate as a separate overall gap that none of the supplied law units provides a case-specific doctrinal test for when a tenant partnership and a separately incorporated company with overlapping personnel, shared premises, mutual agency and separately maintained accounts should be treated as retaining possession versus parting with possession. That unresolved legal bridge is central to L55-L60.

The supplied law set contains no independently supplied authority resolving the appellant's identity-like argument that Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited was 'in truth and reality' the tenant partnership itself, or the respondent's contrary distinct-legal-entity argument. The proposal recognizes the factual dispute but does not identify the absence of such a governing supplied rule as a distinct omission.
